svg.title: Address planning: one allocation tree, three hard rules and three checks that run in CI
svg.desc: Left: the allocation tree from a single block - 239.0.0.0/8 divided by site into a second octet, by service into a third octet, and by channel index into the fourth, so an address can be read aloud and understood. Middle: three hard rules - one group belongs to exactly one PIM mode, service groups must never fall in 224.0.0.0/24 and 232/8 must not be mixed with 239/8, and every address in the network must exist in the source of truth or raise an alert. Right: the three mandatory checks that make the rules executable - MAC collision detection computing 01:00:5e plus the low 23 bits per group, out-of-range detection by ACL audit and source-of-truth validation, and unplanned group detection by diffing periodic show ip mroute snapshots. A bottom band notes that a plan without a script is a document nobody enforces.
svg.text: An address that can be read aloud is an address that survives an outage
The plan is a tree plus a script. The tree makes it readable, the script makes it true.
one octet per site or region, 1..250
The RP mapping must agree on every router.
232/8 and 239/8 are never mixed in one plan.
A group that is not in the source of truth
is an incident, not a discovery.
group. Duplicates in one VLAN fail the build.
Diff periodic show ip mroute snapshots
against the register. Alert on the difference.
All three fit in a pipeline step.
WHAT THE SCRIPT LOOKS LIKE, IN ONE FUNCTION
Note the mask: 0x7f drops the top bit of the second octet. That single bit is why 32 groups share one MAC, and why the check must run per VLAN, not globally.
Run it on every proposed block before allocation, and on every change afterwards.
A plan without a script is a document nobody enforces
The failure is never "we had no plan". It is "the plan lived in a spreadsheet that the last engineer took with them", and the new group was allocated by hand at 2 a.m.
